changelog: Delete C7 — removed the redundant principle about subordinators/contrastive adverbials because it largely duplicates C1 and C3 and distracts from the primary finding about clausal attachments; pruning reduces overlap so the remaining rules can better target cuts before clausal attachments.
findings: The prompt cuts too early when the next segment is a clausal attachment or complement that completes or qualifies what came before, producing contradiction or loss of necessary scope.

diagnosis.why: Deleting C7 removed the explicit discouragement of cutting before subordinators/contrastive adverbials, so the model began inserting more cuts that split subordinate clauses and contrastive phrases. That shift raised agreement at rank‑1 (depth1 +0.556) — helping long‑latency budgets — but degraded deeper ranks (depths 2–3 slightly down) and hurt the short‑latency bins (≤3 and ≤5 showed the largest negative changes of about −0.01), producing the small net drop.
diagnosis.lesson: If you remove the rule discouraging cuts immediately before subordinators/contrastive adverbials, preserve an equivalent constraint for deeper-ranked choices because otherwise the model will create extra intra‑clausal cuts that harm short‑latency (many‑position) performance.
